sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.17,50,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 16-02- 2022.

2. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 16-02-2022 at about 8.45 a.m. when he was travelling as a pillion rider on Daignal Road, 5th Main Junction, Jayanagar 4th Block, Bengaluru city, at that time,
the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-41-P-5271 by driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner, as a result, he sustained injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Jayanagar Orthopaedic center wherein he took treatment.

It is stated that mother/guardian has spent Rs.6 lakhs towards medical expenses and Rs.2,50,000/-
towards conveyance expenses.
3. It is contended that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, studying in 2nd standard and due to accident he was not able to go to the school and lost his academic year.
The accident in question was due to the rash and negligence of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-41-P-5271.

Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer Mohammed Salahuddin vs Sandesh.K.C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184968804/
2 of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4.
On service of notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsels and filed their respective written statements.
5. The respondent No.1 in his objection contended that Car was insured with 2nd respondent which is valid as on the date of accident.

The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exaggerated,
excessive, fanciful speculative and without any legal basis.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the rider of the scooter TVS Jupiter motor cycle bearing No.KA-05-KD-7444.

The driver of the car was carefully driving the car on the date of accident, the rider of the motor cycle suddenly came with high speed and dashed to the front left side bumper of the car which was stopped at the junction.

The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle as the petitioner's mother was riding the motor cycle and petitioner was a pillion rider and both were not wearing the helmet.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
6. The 2nd respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that petition is liable to be dismissed for misjoinder of necessary parties to the proceedings as this respondent has been unnecessarily made as party to the proceedings though the entire negligence is on the part of the third party vehicle bearing No.KA- 05-KD-7444.

The vehicle bearing No.KA-41-P-5271 was covered at the material time under the policy of insurance issued by this respondent subject to the terms,
conditions, exceptions and limitations thereof and confirmation fo the compliance of Sec.64VB of the insurance Act 1938, Motor vehicles Act.
It has also contended that owner and jurisdictional police have not complied the Sec.158(6) and 134(c) of M.V. Act.

Further contended that accident was taken place only due to careless and negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-05-KD-7444, who was riding her motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner, without driving licence and without wearing helmet and allowed a person to carrying on her vehicle more than seating capacity and herself caused the alleged accident.

The petition is liable to dismissed for non joinder of necessary parties i.e., insured and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-KD-7444.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant without any basis.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

7. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 16-02-2022 at about 8.45 a.m., near Daignal road, Jayanagar, 4th block, 5th main junction due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-P- 5271?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

3
3. What order or award?

8. In order to prove the case, the mother/guardian of the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Ex-P1 to Ex-P14, one B. Ramesh-Medical record keeper at Jayanagar Orthopaedic centre got examined as PW-2 and got marked Ex- P15 to 19.
The respondents have not led either oral or documentary evidence.
9. Heard the arguments.
Perused the written arguments submitted by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1.

10. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 filed following citations:-
1. AIR 2003 KAR 258 2. ACJ 2004 ACJ 1827 11.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 ...

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 12. Issues No.1: As per the case of the petitioner that, on 16-02-2022 at about 8.45 a.m. when he was travelling as a pillion rider near 5th main road junction, the rider of the Car bearing No.KA-41-P-5271 drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner, as a result, he sustained injuries all over the body.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined his natural guardian/mother as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, discharge summary, charge sheet, 133 notice, reply to notice, certified copy of ordersheet in CC No.4858/2022, medical bills and school certificate as per Ex.P1 to 14.
13.

According to the version of petitioner the accident happened near Daignal road, Jayanagar, 4th block, 5th main junction, at that time driver of the said car drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P3 to 5 and Ex.P8 it reflects that petitioner was pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing No.KA-05-KD-7444, driver of the vehicle bearing No.KA-41-P-5271, came in a negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle, due to which petitioner sustained injuries.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.

If the driver of bus drove it in a normal speed by observing on moving vehicles on the road,
then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more, the contents of Ex.P.5 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.

Mohammed Salahuddin vs Sandesh.K.C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184968804/
4

Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P8 was also filed as against the driver of the car and also driver of the car has pleaded guilty of the offences charge sheeted against him and paid the fine before the Magistrate court as per Ex.P11.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 to 5 and 11 coupled with Ex.P8 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
14. Even in the instant case the driver of the car is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part.

After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending car bearing registration No.KA- 41-P-5271 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending car bearing Reg. No. KA-41-P-5271.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing No.KA-41-P-5271.
Therefore, minor petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
16. TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:

The natural guardian of the minor petitioner has alleged that due to injuries sustained in the accident, the minor has become permanently disabled and he is not in a position to do the activities which he used to do prior to the accident.
In order to substantiate the same, guardian of the minor petitioner has produced wound certificate, discharge summaries, x-rays, medical bills, school certificate at Ex.P6 to 8, Ex.P12 to 14.
The PW.1 has also examined PW.2 who is the Medical Record keeper and he has produced authorization letter, case sheet, MLC extract, police intimation and x-ray which are marked at Ex.P15 to 19.
It is important to note here that, the guardian of the petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the disability.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation for loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

17. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The wound certificate produced at Ex.P6 reflects that the petitioner has sustained closed fracture BB(L) forearm and Fracture of Olecranon and the doctor has opined that the said injury is grevious in nature.
The Ex-P7 Discharge Summaries of Jayanagar Orthopedic center reveals petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 16-2-2022 to 17-2-2022 and on 07-4-2022 wherein he underwent treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.40,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
18. TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the bills marked at Ex.P12, x-rays at Ex.P13, the PW.1 has spent Rs.59,339/- towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of her cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.

Hence the petitioner is Mohammed Salahuddin vs Sandesh.K.C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184968804/
5 entitled for Rs.59,339/- under the head of medical expenses.
19. TOWARDS DISCOMFORT, INCONVENIENCE AND LOSS OF EARNINGS TO THE PARENTS DURING THE PERIOD OF HOSPITALIZATION :
Looking into the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, a maximum of 4 months would have been required for recovery.
Hence the petitioner's parents could not have attended their work for those long period of 4 months.
Therefore this Tribunal deems it expedient to take note of loss of income of parents during the course of treatment and rest of the petitioner.

The same is quantified at Rs.10,000/-
p.m. and a sum of Rs.40,000/- (10,000 X 4) is awarded as compensation for discomfort, inconvenience and loss of income to the parents during the period of hospitalization of the minor petitioner.
20. ATTENDANT CHARGES, FOOD, NOURISHMENT & TRAVELLING EXPENSES:
The period of hospitalization of 5 days is proved with a help of Ex.P7 discharge summary of Jayanagar orthopaedic centre from 16-2-2022 to 17-2-2022 and on 7-4-2022.
Thus having regard to the age of the petitioner and also the nature of injuries sustained by him, he unavoidably required the service of an attendant for nursing and care.
He must also have been given diet food as suggested by the doctor.

For that the petitioner's family members might have spent some amount towards attendant charges,
food, nourishment & travelling expenses.
Accordingly considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,500/- per day.
is awarded under this head.

21. The calculation table stands follows :

 1 Permanent disability : NIL  2 Pain and Sufferings : 40,000/-

3 Medical expenses : 59,339/-
 4 Discomfort, inconvenience & : 40,000/-
 loss of income to the parents  during the period of  hospitalization  5

Attendant charges, food, : 4,500/-
 nourishment & traveling  expenses  6
Future medical and other : Nil.
incidental expenses

6

In total, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,43,839/-.
22.
The petitioner is claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondents have denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
23. Liability:
Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle bearing No.KA-41-P-5271.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2 nd respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,43,839/-(Rupees One lakh forty three thousand eight hundred and thirty nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount shall be kept in fixed deposit in the name of the minor petitioner in any nationalized bank until he attains the age of majority with a liberty to the guardian of the petitioner to draw periodical interest.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
